subject: Onboarding handoff: Nebula Analytics — model shortlist & traffic projections
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>, Elena Martinez <elena@nebula.ai>
Date: 2026-12-14T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Nebula kickoff — discovery + blockers (handoff)

Priya / Ben / Connor —

Thanks for taking this one on. Quick summary from discovery this morning with Elena at Nebula: product team will use the API to power document Q&A and automated summarization for internal analysts. Key constraints:
- Avg doc length ~4k words (roughly 2.5k–3.5k tokens per document after extraction).
- Typical use is a 1:1 prompt + document retrieval; users may request multi-document summaries in the future.
- Estimated pilot active users: 120 MAU, expected to ramp to ~2,000 MAU over 6 months.
- Security: Nebula requires SOC2 evidence and wants private VPC for production (we'll escalate if needed).

I've attached the discovery notes and their rough MAU file. Next asks for onboarding: model shortlist for pilot vs production, context length recommendations, a conservative token-volume estimate for month 1 and month 6, and a short list of infra/ops items we need to validate before the sandbox (network/VPC, KMS, data retention).

Ben — can you run quick bench tests on the 13B/30B candidates for response latency at 2k token prompts? Connor — please confirm if sandbox VPC will support KV cache and prefix caching (we had a note about a firewall rule).

Elena — thanks again for the time. Priya will be primary CS contact; we'll follow up with a concrete kick-off plan by EOD.

Thanks,
Aditya
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

Attachments: nebula_discovery_notes.pdf, nebula_mau_estimates.csv

From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
To: Elena Martinez <elena@nebula.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-14T11:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Nebula kickoff — discovery + blockers (handoff)

Elena — thanks for the context and the notes, useful. Sharing an initial implementation plan and model shortlist for the pilot + production ramp. High level decisions below; I'll coordinate the detailed perf runs and a small eval set to validate quality tradeoffs. See attached model_recs.xlsx for benchmarks.

1) Pilot (month 0–1): prioritize fast iteration and lower cost. Recommended candidates:
   - RedCloud-7B-Quant (8k context): good latency and cost; acceptable on retrieval-augmented prompts where single-doc answers are primary.
   - Llama-2-13B (16k context): better long-context handling for multi-section docs, slightly higher cost but fewer hallucinations on summarization tasks.

2) Production (month 2+ ramp): keep RedCloud for high-throughput routes; introduce OpenModel-30B-32k for long-context multi-doc summaries and higher-quality generation paths. Pin models per route so we can route by cost/latency.

3) Context length guidance:
   - Single-document Q&A: 8k context sufficient for ~3k-token doc + prompt; aim for 6–8k tokens.
   - Multi-document summarization / chain-of-thought: 24k–32k preferred for combined inputs; use 32k variant on high-value routes.

4) Token volume (conservative engineering estimates):
   - Pilot month (120 MAU, 1.2 calls/user/day avg): ~144 calls/day. Avg request tokens: 3,500 (doc) + 500 (prompt/response) = 4,000 tokens/call.
     -> Pilot tokens/day = 576k tokens/day; tokens/month ≈ 17.3M tokens.
   - Month 6 (2,000 MAU, 1.5 calls/user/day avg): ~3,000 calls/day. Same avg tokens -> 12M tokens/day; tokens/month ≈ 360M tokens.

5) Capacity & SLOs:
   - Pilot: small Dedicated pool (2x A100-equivalent) should keep p95 response latency < 1.2s for 2k-token generation on RedCloud-7B-Quant with batching.
   - Ramp: expect to scale to a 6–8 GPU pool with autoscaling for peak windows; we'll provide more precise GPU-hour estimates after bench runs.

6) Ops checklist:
   - Confirm sandbox VPC + firewall rules (Connor)
   - SOC2 evidence packet & SAML config (security/compliance)
   - Token retention and logging policy for the sandbox (Ben)

Next steps: Ben to run latency/cost bench on RedCloud-7B-Quant and Llama-2-13B with 2k and 4k token prompts by 2026-12-18. Connor to validate sandbox VPC network path and KV cache support by 2026-12-17. I'll draft a short eval set for summarization tests and share by EOD.

Elena — any immediate constraints on redaction or PII handling we should add to the checklist?

Thanks,
Priya Natarajan
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

Attachments: model_recs.xlsx

From: Elena Martinez <elena@nebula.ai>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Procurement <procurement@nebula.ai>
Date: 2026-12-15T10:07:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Nebula kickoff — discovery + blockers (handoff)

Thanks Priya — this looks good and thorough. Couple quick clarifications from our side before you run benches:

1) For multi-document summaries, our internal workflows typically concatenate 3–5 shorter docs (avg 1k words each) rather than one very large doc. Would you still recommend the 24k–32k path or is 16k a reasonable middle ground for initial production?

2) On token volume: can you provide a simple cost ballpark for 17M tokens/month vs 360M tokens/month assuming RedCloud-7B-Quant for pilot and OpenModel-30B-32k for production? We just need a rough number to include in our internal budget exercise.

3) PII: we'll start with redaction on ingestion, but procurement also asked about data retention windows for logs — our default ask is 90 days. Is that compatible with sandbox defaults?

If those are reasonable, procurement and I will align timelines internally and we can lock the sandbox start for the week of 12/20.

Best,
Elena Martinez
Head of Data Products, Nebula Analytics

From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Martinez <elena@nebula.ai>
Date: 2026-12-16T16:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Nebula kickoff — discovery + blockers (handoff)

All — quick replies inline and next-action assignment.

Elena: short answers up front —
1) Multi-doc concat: start with 16k for the first production tier as a middle ground; we recommend a staged rollout to 32k only for high-value routes (cost overhead is non-linear). We'll include 16k vs 32k quality delta in the bench notes.
2) Cost ballpark (very rough, includes model inference only, not storage/network):
   - Pilot (RedCloud-7B-Quant, 17M tokens/month): ~$1.5k–2k/month (inference compute only).
   - Production ramp (OpenModel-30B-32k, 360M tokens/month): ~$45k–55k/month.
   These are order-of-magnitude numbers — Ben's bench runs will give per-token run-time that we can convert to GPU-hour and then to a more accurate monthly cost.
3) Retention: sandbox default 90 days for logs is compatible; for production we'll need to confirm retention policy in the Private deployment contract.

Assignments & timeline:
- Ben: bench runs on RedCloud-7B-Quant (2k/4k token prompts) and Llama-2-13B (2k tokens); include latency, p50/p95, and token/sec. Due 2026-12-18.
- Connor: confirm sandbox VPC + KV cache + firewall rules; verify KMS path for temporary credentials. Due 2026-12-17.
- Priya (me): share eval prompts + docs for summarization by 2026-12-14 EOD (done) and curate a 12-sample eval set by 2026-12-18.
- Aditya: follow up on procurement timelines (Procurement has been looped).

I'll prepare a short one-pager (ramp plan + model routing recommendations) for Elena and procurement to review; target to share by 2026-12-17 AM. Once benches are in, we'll convert to a recommended Dedicated pool size and provide a GPU-hour estimate for their budget.

Elena — appreciate the quick turnaround. If 12/20 sandbox start looks good from your side, we'll lock dates after Ben/Connor confirm the sandbox readiness.

Thanks everyone,
Priya
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

Attachments: sla_ramp_plan.docx
